transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... things at work have been feeling off. Like people are watching what I buy, vendors too, and the launch numbers keep getting messed with so I look stupid. My supervisor says the reports don’t show that, but I still can’t really shake it.
How long have you been feeling this way—that people are watching you and messing with your numbers?
I don’t know exactly… maybe around ten months. It’s been going on a while.
Over these past ten months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other end, unusually elevated, energetic, or needing much less sleep?

Yeah… I guess the sleep part, yeah. There’ve been weeks where I only sleep like three or four hours, but I wake up feeling… wired, like I’m good to go. Lying there feels pointless, like I should be using the time to get things done.
During times when you're not feeling that wired, high-energy state—when your mood and sleep are more normal—do you still feel that people are watching you or messing with your numbers?

Yeah… it didn’t totally go away. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping more normal, not feeling like I was… running everything or whatever. But I still thought people were tracking my buys for a few weeks. And… I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom sometimes.

Out of the full 10 months, about how many weeks did you have those psychotic experiences—like feeling watched or hearing the voice—while your mood and sleep were completely normal, without any of the high-energy or manic periods?
Maybe… a few weeks. I wasn’t all wired then, and I was sleeping more normal, but I still thought they were tracking my buys. And I’d still hear the voice sometimes in the stockroom.
Out of the full 10 months, roughly how many weeks total would you say you were in that high-energy, low-sleep state, compared to the rest of the time?

I don’t know exactly… but probably most of it, honestly. Like a lot of those months I was in that wired or irritated mode, working too much and feeling like I knew what I was doing and people couldn’t really slow me down. There were calmer parts, but they were shorter.

Yeah… like I said, most of the time since it started was those wired or irritated stretches. Working too much, feeling really sure of myself, not really letting people slow me down. The calmer times were there, but they were shorter.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms psychotic symptoms (being watched, auditory hallucinations) occurred during a distinct period of a few weeks without mood symptoms (satisfying the criterion for schizoaffective disorder), while manic symptoms with decreased need for sleep, increased energy, and grandiosity dominated the majority of the 10-month illness course. This pattern—mood episode present for majority of illness duration with psychosis also present in the absence of mood symptoms—fits schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, and argues against schizophrenia (F20.0), which requires mood symptoms to be brief relative to the psychotic illness.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a ~10-month illness course featuring concurrent psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions about being monitored/tracked, auditory hallucinations in the stockroom) and a manic-like mood syndrome (markedly decreased need for sleep, elevated energy, grandiosity, irritability, increased goal-directed activity) that co-occurred for the majority of the episode. Critically, there was also a distinct period of at least several weeks where psychotic symptoms (delusions of being tracked, auditory hallucinations) persisted in the absence of any mood episode, satisfying the requirement for hallucinations/delusions for ≥2 weeks without prominent mood symptoms. Because mood symptoms (manic) were present for the majority of the total duration of the psychotic illness, and psychotic symptoms occurred both during and independent of the mood episode, this pattern is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0) rather than Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychotic symptoms only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief relative to total illness duration).
